title: Verifier classes and workload capabilities
canonical_definition: Support independently typed classes such as protocol verifier, independent verifier, job-owner verifier, oracle verifier, TEE verifier and committee verifier.

milestone_relationship.rationale: Identity/lifecycle and class/workload capability are now separable; broader app-specific integration waits until exact versioned verification policy is added in CMP-1.4.3.

implementation.workload_binding: Exact nonzero bytes32 workloadClass; no wildcard or implicit inheritance.
implementation.eligibility: Exact verifier ID, current authority, current verifier revision, class and workload tuple must all match; verifier identity must be ACTIVE.

authority_boundaries: Class/workload qualification does not appoint a verifier to a job.
Class/workload qualification does not prove beneficial-owner independence or objective correctness.
Class/workload qualification does not publish or rewrite a verification policy.
Class/workload qualification grants no Vault custody, settlement, beneficiary redirection, stake/slash, worker, governance, validator, bridge or arbitrary-wallet authority.
Each verifier class and workload tuple is independently enabled/revoked with versioned evidence.
Suspended or retired verifier identities fail closed even when historical capability qualification exists.
exit_criteria: All six canonical initial verifier classes are represented as distinct typed identifiers.
Verifier capabilities are bound to exact workload-class identifiers.
Class/workload tuples can be independently qualified and revoked with immutable revision history.
Eligibility requires an ACTIVE exact-current verifier identity and exact class/workload tuple.
Unknown classes, zero workloads, zero evidence, unauthorized mutation and retired verifier mutation fail closed.
No unrelated authority is granted by capability qualification.
